title: 2014 AMC 12A Problem 22
statement: The number \(5^{867}\) is between \(2^{2013}\) and \(2^{2014}.\) How many pairs of integers \((m,n)\) are there such that \(1\le m\le2012\) and \[5^n\lt2^m\lt2^{m+2}\lt5^{n+1}?\]

solutions.text:
Because \(2^2\lt5\lt2^3,\) each interval \((5^n,5^{n+1})\) contains either two or three powers of \(2.\) The chain \(5^n\lt2^m\lt2^{m+2}\lt5^{n+1}\) holds exactly when the interval contains three consecutive powers of \(2,\) and then there is a unique such \(m.\)

Let \(d\) and \(t\) be the numbers of intervals \((5^n,5^{n+1})\) for \(0\le n\le866\) containing two and three powers of \(2,\) respectively. Since \(2^{2013}\lt5^{867}\lt2^{2014}\) there are \(2013\) powers of \(2\) in total, giving \(d+t=867\) and \(2d+3t=2013.\)

Solving, \(t=2013-2\cdot867=279.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Between consecutive powers \(5^n\) and \(5^{n+1}\) there are either two or three powers of \(2\)
The inequality asks for three such powers; if \(d,t\) count the two-power and three-power gaps, then \(d+t=867\) and \(2d+3t=2013\)
